instructions: goemail is a production Go email library (module github.com/KARTIKrocks/goemail, package name email). Everything composes around the Sender interface (Send, Close); Mailer, SMTPSender, MockSender, middleware, the connection pool, and AsyncSender all implement or wrap it. This is a five-module repo: root (dependency-light: only golang.org/x/sync and golang.org/x/time) plus providers/sendgrid, providers/mailgun, providers/ses, providers/otelmail as separate modules so core users don't pull in the AWS SDK / OTel transitively. Treat this as a security-sensitive library: it builds raw SMTP/MIME messages and signs them with DKIM, both classic injection and crypto-correctness risk surfaces. Prioritize correctness, security (header/CRLF injection, DKIM signing, TLS defaults), and concurrency safety (pool, async workers, middleware) over style — skip anything golangci-lint already enforces. See AGENTS.md for repo conventions and .greptile/rules.md for pattern rationale grounded in this library's own security fixes.

rules.rule: Any code path that writes a caller- or template-supplied string into an email header or the raw message (custom headers, Subject, From/To/Cc/Bcc/Reply-To, attachment filenames/content-types) must reject or strip CR/LF before it reaches the wire, matching the existing protection in Email.Validate/AddHeader. Never add a header-writing path that bypasses AddHeader's canonicalization and CRLF check, and never assume net/mail.ParseAddress having already run makes a value safe to emit unmodified — a value that fails to parse must be sanitized, not passed through.

DKIM signing (dkim.go) implements RFC 6376/8463 canonicalization (relaxed/simple header and body canon), header folding/unfolding, and body-hash trailing-CRLF handling. A change to canonicalizeHeader, canonicalizeBody, removeTrailingEmptyLines, buildDKIMTagList, or signData must preserve exact RFC-specified byte behavior — a subtly wrong canonicalization produces a signature that verifies for the wrong bytes, or fails silently at the receiving mail server with no local test failure. Flag any such change that isn't backed by a spec citation or a test vector.

SMTP/TLS connection setup (SMTPSender and the pool's dialer) must not allow InsecureSkipVerify or a TLS version below 1.2 outside of a test-only code path, and STARTTLS must be negotiated before AUTH is sent. Flag any relaxation of these defaults even if gated behind a config flag, unless the flag is explicitly named/documented as test/insecure-only.

Every *pooledConn obtained from smtpPool.get/dial/tryGetIdle/waitForConn must be returned to the pool or closed on every path, including error and cancellation paths — a leaked pooled connection is a slow resource exhaustion bug, not a style nit. A waiter registered in waitForConn must be reliably removed (cancelWaiter) so a canceled caller doesn't leave a stale channel the pool later tries to hand a connection to.

AsyncSender's worker goroutines must have a visible termination path tied to Close() (a closed channel or context they select on), and Close must not return until in-flight/queued work has been drained or explicitly discarded per its documented contract. A goroutine that can outlive Close(), or a Send/SendWait after Close that blocks forever instead of returning ErrQueueClosed, is a bug.

Mailer.Send/SendEmail/SendBatch must deep-copy the caller-supplied Email (cloneEmail) before mutating or handing it to a Sender, and must not let one goroutine's in-flight send observe mutations from a concurrent caller reusing the same Email/slice/map. This was a real bug (see CHANGELOG 0.2.0) — flag any new Mailer method or middleware that reads/writes an *Email without going through the existing copy path.

New failure conditions should use or extend the existing sentinel-error style (var Err... = errors.New("email: ...")) and the Error type (Op/From/To/wrapped err), checked via errors.Is/errors.As — not ad hoc string-matched errors. Provider adapters must translate their HTTP/SDK errors into this same shape rather than leaking a provider-specific error type across the Sender boundary.

Provider adapters (providers/sendgrid, providers/mailgun, providers/ses) must propagate the caller's context into every HTTP/SDK call, always close response bodies, treat non-2xx responses as errors with enough detail to debug (not swallowed), and never log API keys, secrets, or full message bodies.

The root module (files directly in the repository root) must stay dependency-light: only the standard library, golang.org/x/sync, and golang.org/x/time. A new third-party dependency (an SDK, an HTTP client wrapper, etc.) belongs in a providers/ sub-module, never in root go.mod.
